pad_cell_behavior.source: simulations/OSS_FRAME_GIO.spice -- OSS_FRAME_GIO instantiates one OSS_ESD_5V_DIO(VDD,PAD,VSS,HIZ,OUT) per pad
pad_cell_behavior.HIZ: HIZ=1 (tied VDD) => output driver disabled, pad is Hi-Z / input-only. HIZ=0 (tied VSS) => output driver enabled, pad is actively driven by OUT. Derived from transistor-level trace (MXM9-MXM20), not from a naming guess.
pad_cell_behavior.OUT: data driven onto PAD when HIZ=0 (driver enabled). Irrelevant (don't-care) when HIZ=1.
pad_cell_behavior.note_sda: The SDA pad implements a correct open-drain I2C output: its OUT<n> pin is permanently tied to VSS (so the driver, when enabled, only ever pulls SDA LOW -- SDA is never actively driven high by this device), and its HIZ<n> is dynamically driven by core.sda_oe. core.sda_oe is ACTIVE-LOW ('assert drive': sda_oe=0 => actively pull SDA low, sda_oe=1 => release/Hi-Z), confirmed against src/i2c_slave_async.v (see open_questions_resolved).

_meta.dis_net_resolved: 'DIS' is a real, intentionally-used net: P7's pad is daisy-chained together with a fixed-COUNT set of HIZ pins (originally HIZ1,HIZ3,HIZ4,HIZ5,HIZ6,HIZ11,HIZ12,HIZ14 -- 9 points total including P7), one shared net, routed as sequential links purely to save wire (script/route_gio_core.py's DIS_CHAIN_POINTS/DIS_LINKS), not a directional 'P7 drives' relationship. Not tied to VDD or VSS anywhere -- its logic level is set externally by whatever the tester/board drives onto pad P7. Membership is NOT fixed silicon -- it's drawn metal (see route_gio_core_v9.py's own header), so it moves with whichever pads are assigned the 'plain bidirectional data pin' role; see pad_reassignment_2026_08_31 for the one-member swap (HIZ1 out, HIZ13 in) needed by the new pad assignment.

pad_reassignment_2026_08_31._comment: User-requested reassignment (this session): 'P1<P2, P2<P13, P3<P14, P4<P3, P5<P1, P6<P4, P11<P12, P12<P11, P13<P5, P14<P6' -- read as 'new pad <- old pad's whole role (core signal + its HIZ/OUT behavior template)'. Net effect: SCL and SDA move from their old (non-adjacent) pads P2/P13 onto adjacent pads P1/P2; the 8 tx_data/rx_data bit pads get shuffled among P3/P4/P5/P6/P11/P12/P13/P14 (each bit's tx+rx pair always stays on ONE shared physical pad, matching the pre-existing convention). P7/P9/P10/P15 unaffected (not part of the user's list).
pad_reassignment_2026_08_31.dis_chain_membership_change: HIZ1 leaves the DIS chain (P1 is now the plain-Hi-Z-always SCL pad); HIZ13 joins it (P13 is now a plain DIS-chain data pad). Chain still has exactly 9 points (P7 + 8 HIZ pins), same as before -- just one member swapped. HIZ13 (921.7,220,RIGHT) sits naturally between HIZ14 (921.7,580) and HIZ12 (921.7,-220), already-adjacent chain members on the same RIGHT edge, so the chain's physical path needs only a small local edit, not a redesign.

routability_check.method: Re-ran route_gio_core_v9.py's own exact shared-pool lane-assignment algorithm (perimeter_s / unroll / greedy interval-to-lane packing, R_NOM=880, CUT=4625, PERI=7400, MARGIN=5.0) with the new gio-side endpoints substituted (core-side pin positions are fixed and never change -- only which physical pad/HIZ/OUT pin each signal targets changes). New endpoint coordinates read directly from LEF/OSS_FRAME_GIO.lef's real PIN RECT geometry (see pad_pin_coords above), not guessed. Verified the replicated algorithm reproduces the documented baseline (11 lanes) exactly before trusting its output on the new assignment.
routability_check.result: 10 lanes needed for the new assignment (vs 11 for the current/old assignment) -- FEWER, not more. Max lane radius = 901.0um vs the hard physical ceiling NEAR_R=913.0um (12.0um of clearance, actually 6.0um MORE margin than the current design's own 6.0um). No lane-budget or geometry problem.
routability_check.dis_chain: Separate, uncongested radius (DIS_R=840.0, well below the signal-lane band 847-901) -- the one-member swap does not interact with or add pressure to the signal-lane budget at all.
routability_check.conclusion: ROUTABLE with the existing algorithm and infrastructure, and slightly MORE comfortable (fewer lanes, more margin) than today's layout. No blocking issue found.
